limitations: A runner who never runs hard is usually under-estimated; evidence coverage (a heuristic label) shows how thin the evidence is. Noisy GPS distance, downhill courses and short fast segments can over-estimate.
Runs over 42.5 km (ultras) and under 3 km do not contribute to MMR at all; they are shown as distance evidence only.
Riegel's single exponent fits some runners better than others; endurance types convert optimistically from long runs and speed types from short ones.
No elevation adjustment: summary ascent does not describe the route. Hilly runs are flagged; net-downhill courses cannot be detected and may overstate.
Heart rate and perceived exertion are displayed only. GPS errors move the estimate about one-for-one.
The recency rate, grace period and 365-day window are assumptions, not measured detraining.
Not validated against real race results; the points scale is a convention.
meaning: Running MMR estimates your current running ability from your own activities. No opponents or races needed.
Ability is expressed as a 10 km-equivalent time (Riegel conversion, k = 1.06), using Run activities of 3 to 42.5 km only. Longer and shorter runs are kept and shown as distance-specific evidence.

Effort is usually unknown, so no single run is read as your maximum and an easier run never lowers MMR. The estimate is your best converted evidence in the last 365 days; the conversion is itself an estimate.
Older evidence counts gradually slower (a documented recency assumption: 1.5 % per 30 days after 30 days).

Effort labels (easy, hard, race) are context only: changing a label never changes MMR (mmr-envelope-v2; the v1 rule that let a hard/race label lower older evidence was removed on 2026-10-22). A recent hard or race label that agrees with the estimate can raise the evidence-coverage label from medium to high.

Points: 3000 × ln(7200 s / T10) / ln(7200 / 1560). 10 km in 2:00:00 = 0, 1:00:00 ≈ 1360, 50:00 ≈ 1717, 40:00 ≈ 2155, 30:00 ≈ 2719, 26:00 = 3000. A fixed mapping (about 20 points per 1 % of speed), never rescaled by who else is imported; not a population ranking, not a validated ability scale, not Elo win probabilities.
